# Read QC and Preprocessing

Domain knowledge for short-read quality control, trimming, and
read-level filtering tasks.

## Expected Workflow

1. Check the input facts first:
   - single-end or paired-end
   - read length
   - expected adapters or library type
   - whether the task is trimming, contamination removal, or both
2. Choose the lightest preprocessing that solves the actual problem.
3. Verify that quality improves after trimming instead of assuming it did.
4. If reads are being removed against a reference, define exactly what
   “retained” means before running the filter.
5. Accept the branch only if the outputs and reports describe the same
   retained-read definition.

read_ee <- function(file, trunc) {
  con <- gzfile(file, 'rt'); on.exit(close(con))
  ees <- numeric(); lens <- integer(); n <- 0L
  repeat {
    h <- readLines(con, n=1)
    if (length(h) == 0) break
    seq <- readLines(con, n=1); plus <- readLines(con, n=1); qual <- readLines(con, n=1)
    n <- n + 1L
    if (n > 5000) break
    qchars <- strsplit(substr(qual, 1, min(trunc, nchar(qual))), '', fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
    qs <- utf8ToInt(paste0(qchars, collapse='')) - 33L
    ees[n] <- sum(10"'^(-qs/10))
    lens[n] <- nchar(seq)
  }
  quantile(ees, probs=c(.1,.25,.5,.75,.9,.95,.99), na.rm=TRUE)
}
for (mate in c('"'forward','reverse')) {
  cat('\\n', mate, '\\n', sep='')
  vals <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(list.dirs('data/inputs/paired_input_data', recursive=FALSE, full.names=TRUE)), function(d) {
    file <- if (mate=='forward') file.path(d,'forward','forward.fastqsanger.gz') else file.path(d,'reverse','reverse.fastqsanger.gz')
    trunc <- if (mate=='forward') 240 else 200
    q <- read_ee(file, trunc)
    data.frame(sample=basename(d), t(q), check.names=FALSE)
  }))
  print(vals, row.names=FALSE)
}
RS"
